claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a high-temperature BCC state.
Ni and Al diffuse faster than the other alloying elements in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 during cooling and intermediate-temperature exposure.
Slower cooling permits local segregation of Ni and Al.
Isothermal holds at 500–600 °C permit local segregation and ordering of Ni and Al.
Preferential Ni and Al segregation produces local short-range chemical order.
Ni- and Al-associated compositional fluctuations lower the nucleation barrier for ordered precipitates.
Short-range ordering catalyzes nucleation of B2 or FCC secondary regions within the BCC matrix.
Diffusional partitioning during slow cooling or isothermal holding transforms the disordered BCC state into a multiphase structure containing B2 or FCC regions.
Rapid quenching suppresses Ni/Al segregation and short-range ordering.
Rapid quenching preserves a predominantly disordered BCC structure.
Slowly cooled and isothermally held samples will have a higher volume fraction of B2 or FCC secondary phases than rapidly quenched samples.
XRD, TEM, and atom-probe tomography can detect the predicted phase and compositional differences.
The proposed mechanism operates around 500–600 °C because diffusion is active in that temperature range.
The proposed mechanism may cease to operate at very low temperatures because atomic mobility is insufficient.
Competing phase transformations may prevent the proposed mechanism from controlling the observed behavior.

contradictions.description: FCC is repeatedly grouped with B2 as an 'ordered' phase, although FCC denotes a lattice type and is not by itself evidence of chemical ordering. The hypothesis does not identify a specific ordered FCC derivative or ordering signature, making the claimed ordered-FCC outcome internally ambiguous.
